i0: Use **comparatives** to compare two things (*Toronto is **bigger than** Ottawa*) and **superlatives** to say which is the most in a group (*It's **the biggest** city in Canada*).
i1: This page also covers *as… as* and how to make a comparison stronger or weaker (*much bigger, a bit cheaper, by far the best*).
cs-forms.t: Bigger, more expensive, the biggest, the most expensive
cs-forms.s: Short adjectives take **-er / the -est** (*cheap → cheaper → the cheapest*). Long adjectives take **more / the most** (*expensive → more expensive → the most expensive*). Use **than** after a comparative.
cs-forms.b1: Use ***than*** after a comparative: *My brother is taller **than** me.* Use ***the*** before a superlative, often with *in* or *of*: *the tallest **in** the class, the best day **of** my life*.
cs-forms.b2: Some two-syllable adjectives can take both forms: *quieter / more quiet, simpler / more simple, cleverer / more clever*.
cs-irregular.t: Good, better, best; bad, worse, worst; far, further
cs-irregular.s: Irregular forms: **good → better → the best**, **bad → worse → the worst**, **far → farther / further → the farthest / the furthest**. The adverbs **well** and **badly** also become **better** and **worse**.
cs-irregular.b1: ***Further*** also means **more, extra**: *For **further** information, call us.* (not *farther* here)
cs-as-as.t: As… as, not as… as, the same as
cs-as-as.s: Use ***as + adjective + as*** to say two things are **equal**: *She's as tall as her mother.* ***Not as / not so… as*** = less: *Ottawa isn't as big as Toronto.* Use ***the same as*** for things that are equal.
cs-as-as.b0.1.1: *This hotel **isn't as expensive as** the other one.*
cs-as-as.b0.2.1: *Your phone is **the same as** mine. She's **the same age as** me.*
cs-as-as.b0.4.1: *Their house is **twice as big as** ours.*
cs-as-as.b1: After *as… as*, everyday English uses an object pronoun: *as tall as **me***. Careful English: *as tall as **I am***.
cs-modifying.t: Much bigger, a bit cheaper, by far the best
cs-modifying.s: Make comparatives stronger with ***much, a lot, far*** (*much bigger*) and weaker with ***a bit, a little, slightly*** (*a bit cheaper*). Make superlatives stronger with ***by far*** (*by far the best*).
cs-modifying.b0.3.1: *It's **even** colder today.* (and it was already cold)
cs-modifying.b1: Don't use ***very*** with comparatives: *much better* (not *very better*).
cs-modifying.b2: ***Even*** + comparative shows the first thing was already high: *Yesterday was hot, but today is **even hotter**.*
x.cs-modifying-s03: A small difference: *a bit more expensive*.
x.cs-forms-b01: Most two-syllable adjectives that don't end in *-y* use *more*: *more modern*.
x.cs-modifying-b01: A small difference: *a bit more slowly*.
